newsitem.title: UK: Brokers could feel squeeze of technology - SIB chief.
newsitem.headline: Brokers could feel squeeze of technology - SIB chief.

text.p: Modern technology is likely to lead to more direct securities trading which could squeeze intermediaries such as brokers, Andrew Large, head of the Securities and Investments Board, said on Tuesday.

Enhancements to current technology which will provide more secure, efficient and faster systems will open up the market-place, he added, and this greater accessibility clearly points to greater potential for direct trading.
"The commercial implication of that is obvious: intermediaries will need to be quick on their toes if they're not to be squeezed," Large said.
In regulatory terms, a system which has tended to exercise leverage at the intermediary level could start to be called into question, Large added.
Potentially the greatest challenge facing financial market regulators is changing technology which, if properly used, could make safer markets and provide greater investor protection.
Large said it was important to find solutions that work to support progress rather than impede it.
"(Technology) can speed order input, cut settlement times create audit trails, and reduce the scope for human error - and mischief," Large said in a speech at the "Big Bang: Ten Years on' conference.
Large said other implications of the technological revolution include the role and ownership of exchanges and the enforcement powers of regulators.
He recognised there was increasing frustration with the current system and said an extended system of greater civil powers could be an alternative, while not wanting to decriminalise market abuse.
